description: Saskatoon piloted waste diversion programs in public spaces and events.
Pilots tested multi-stream bins, AI sorting, and reusable foodware.
Future plans aim to reduce public space waste to landfill.

chips.text: Mayor Bulk noted high contamination in blue bins after decades.
Three Business Improvement Districts participated in pilot programs.
Public surveys showed barriers like receptacle availability and cleanliness.
Reusable foodware pilot considered cultural practices of Indigenous peoples.
City aims for 70% waste diversion from landfill.
A multi-phase waste diversion approach report is due in Q2 this year.

description: City explores leasing office space on urban reserves.
Addresses space needs and advances reconciliation commitments.
Supports Indigenous employees exercising treaty rights.

chips.text: Councillor Geller linked urban reserve leases to Indigenous treaty rights.
Taxpayers could face increased costs for new leases.
Saskatoon would be the first city to pursue urban reserve leases.
No strategy exists to accommodate all Indigenous employees on reserves.
Administration will continue evaluating urban reserve leasing options.
